chapter.li: LEChapter20 Verse1 The first day of the week, Mary Magdalene comes early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulcher, and saw the stone taken away from the sepulcher and two angels sitting thereon. VerseEnd Verse2 Then she runs and comes to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and says unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulcher and we know not where they have laid him. VerseEnd Verse3 Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulcher. VerseEnd Verse4 So they ran both together, and the other disciple did outrun Peter and came first to the sepulcher. VerseEnd Verse5 And he, stooping down and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying there, yet went he not in. VerseEnd Verse6 Then comes Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulcher, and sees the linen clothes lying there, VerseEnd Verse7 and the napkin that was about his head not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself. VerseEnd Verse8 Then went in also that other disciple who came first to the sepulcher, and he saw and believed VerseEnd — Verse9 for as yet they knew not the scripture that he must rise again from the dead. VerseEnd Verse10 Then the disciples went away again unto their own home. VerseEnd

Verse11 But Mary stood outside at the sepulcher, weeping. And as she wept, she stooped down and looked into the sepulcher, VerseEnd Verse12 and sees two angels in white sitting, the one at the head and the other at the feet where the body of Jesus had lain. VerseEnd Verse13 And they said unto her, Woman, why do you weep? She says unto them, Because they have taken away my Lord and I know not where they have laid him. VerseEnd Verse14 And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus. VerseEnd Verse15 Jesus says unto her, Woman, why do you weep? Whom do you seek? She, supposing him to be the gardener, says unto him, Sir, if you have borne him from here, tell me where you have laid him and I will take him away. VerseEnd Verse16 Jesus says unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and says unto him, Rabboni — which is to say, Master. VerseEnd Verse17 Jesus says unto her, Hold me not, for I am not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brethren and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God. VerseEnd Verse18 Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord and that he had spoken these things unto her. VerseEnd

Verse19 Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples had assembled for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and says unto them, Peace be unto you. VerseEnd Verse20 And when he had so said, he showed unto them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad when they saw the Lord. VerseEnd Verse21 Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you. As my Father has sent me, even so send I you. VerseEnd Verse22 And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and says unto them, Receive the holy ghost. VerseEnd Verse23 Whoever’s sins you remit, they are remitted unto them, and whoever’s sins you retain, they are retained. VerseEnd

Verse24 But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. VerseEnd Verse25 The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe. VerseEnd Verse26 And after eight days, again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them. Then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst and said, Peace be unto you. VerseEnd Verse27 Then says he to Thomas, Reach here your finger and behold my hands, and reach here your hand and thrust it into my side, and be not faithless, but believing. VerseEnd Verse28 And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God. VerseEnd Verse29 Jesus says unto him, Thomas, because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are they that have not seen and yet have believed. VerseEnd

Verse30 And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book. VerseEnd Verse31 But these are written, that you might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that, believing, you might have life through his name. VerseEnd LEChapter21 Verse1 After these things, Jesus showed himself again to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias; and in this way he showed himself: VerseEnd Verse2 There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples. VerseEnd Verse3 Simon Peter says unto them, I go fishing. They say unto him, We also go with you. They went forth and entered into a ship immediately, and that night they caught nothing. VerseEnd

Verse4 But when the morning had now come, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. VerseEnd Verse5 Then Jesus says unto them, Children, do you have any food? They answered him, No. VerseEnd Verse6 And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship and you shall find. They cast, therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes. VerseEnd Verse7 Therefore, that disciple whom Jesus loved says unto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girded his fisher’s coat unto him (for he was naked) and did cast himself into the sea. VerseEnd Verse8 And the other disciples came in a little ship (for they were not far from land, but about two hundred cubits) dragging the net with fishes. VerseEnd

Verse9 As soon then as they had come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread. VerseEnd Verse10 Jesus says unto them, Bring of the fish which you have now caught. VerseEnd Verse11 Simon Peter went up and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, a hundred fifty-three. And for all there were, so many, yet was not the net broken. VerseEnd

Verse12 Jesus says unto them, Come and dine. And none of the disciples dared ask him, Who are you? — knowing that it was the Lord. VerseEnd Verse13 Jesus then comes and takes bread and gives them, and fish likewise. VerseEnd Verse14 This is now the third time that Jesus showed himself to his disciples after he had risen from the dead. VerseEnd

Verse15 So when they had dined, Jesus says to Simon Peter, Simon son of Jona, do you love me more than these? He says unto him, Yea, Lord, you know that I love you. He says unto him, Feed my lambs. VerseEnd Verse16 He says to him again the second time, Simon son of Jona, do you love me? He says unto him, Yea, Lord, you know that I love you. He says unto him, Feed my sheep. VerseEnd Verse17 He says unto him the third time, Simon son of Jona, do you love me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Do you love me? And he said unto him, Lord, you know all things. You know that I love you. Jesus says unto him, Feed my sheep. VerseEnd

Verse18 Truly, truly I say unto you, when you were young, you girded yourself and walked where you desired. But when you shall be old, you shall stretch forth your hands and another shall gird you and carry you where you desire not. VerseEnd Verse19 This he spoke, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he says unto him, Follow me. VerseEnd

Verse20 Then Peter, turning about, sees the disciple whom Jesus loved, following — who also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, which is he that betrays you? VerseEnd Verse21 Peter, seeing him, says to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do? VerseEnd Verse22 Jesus says unto him, If I desire that he remain until I come, what is that to you? Follow me. VerseEnd Verse23 Then went this saying abroad among the brethren — that that disciple should not die. Yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die, but, If I desire that he remain until I come, what is that to you? VerseEnd
Verse24 This is the disciple who testifies of these things, and wrote these things. And we know that his testimony is true. VerseEnd

Verse25 And there are also many other things which Jesus did, which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen. VerseEnd
